#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1644 — update_git_mirror.sh self-test                                  ║
# ║  The contract closes the run-38855793382 incident ("Update local git      ║
# ║  mirrors" died exit 128 — "error: 2931 bytes of body are still            ║
# ║  expected"): the old inline workflow logic fetched ONCE (stderr            ║
# ║  swallowed), fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h       ║
# ║  transfer died mid-flight, and had no retry and no partial-dir cleanup.   ║
# ║  Scenarios (local file:// fixture remotes, fault-injected `git` shim):    ║
# ║    T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror                                ║
# ║    T2 fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits                     ║
# ║    T3 a poisoned partial mirror dir is recovered (recreate)               ║
# ║    T4 THE INCIDENT: transient fetch failure + armed clone failure —       ║
# ║        a fetch RETRY must recover with NO recreate (the legacy logic      ║
# ║        recreated, hit the failing clone and died exit 128)                ║
# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║
# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║
# ║    T7 fetch-retry exhaustion falls back to a successful recreate          ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy
#   --legacy runs the incident scenarios against the PRE-FIX inline
#   workflow logic (embedded below, verbatim behavior of the old
#   build-macos.yml step): every scenario PASSES iff the legacy logic
#   FAILS the contract — i.e. the bug is reproduced. Zero legacy failures
#   means the repro is broken.

cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
MODE="${1:-}"
SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  echo "❌ $SCRIPT missing — run this selftest from the repo root" >&2
  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong
# (the wrapper re-resolves `git` via PATH back into the shim) and spin.
# `command -v -p` resolves against the system default PATH.
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi

pass=0
fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"
  if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
    git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
  else
    if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
    fi
  fi
}

update_mirror() {
  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
  else
    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
  fi
}

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {
  local dir="$1" fail_fetch="$2" fail_clone="$3"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  echo "$fail_fetch" > "$dir/fetch_left"
  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"
  cat > "$dir/git" <<SHIM
#!/usr/bin/env bash
REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
sub=""; skip=0
for a in "\$@"; do
  if [ "\$skip" = 1 ]; then skip=0; continue; fi
  case "\$a" in
    -c|-C) skip=1 ;;
    -*) ;;
    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;
  esac
done
case "\$sub" in
  fetch)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/fetch_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
  clone)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/clone_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
esac
exec "\$REAL_GIT" "\$@"
SHIM
  chmod +x "$dir/git"
}

use_shim() {  # $1 = shim dir ("" = restore real git)
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then PATH="$1:$REAL_PATH"; else PATH="$REAL_PATH"; fi
}

# ── fixture: a local bare "origin" ──────────────────────────────────────────
make_fixture() {
  local d="$1"
  git init -q "$d/work"
  git -C "$d/work" config user.email t@example.com
  git -C "$d/work" config user.name t
  echo one > "$d/work/file.txt"
  git -C "$d/work" add .
  git -C "$d/work" commit -qm one
  git clone -q --bare "$d/work" "$d/remote.git"
}

advance_fixture() {  # $1 = fixture root — one more commit on the remote
  git -C "$1/work" commit -qm "two-$RANDOM" --allow-empty
  git -C "$1/work" push -q "$1/remote.git" HEAD
}

mirror_head() { git -C "$1" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | head -1; }

export REAL_PATH="$PATH"
export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0

# ══ T1: fresh clone creates a working mirror ════════════════════════════════
t1() {
  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
    ok "T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T1 fresh clone FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T2: fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits ═════════════════════
t2() {
  local d="$WORK/t2"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local before after
  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
  advance_fixture "$d"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  after=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$before" != "$after" ]; then
    ok "T2 fetch advances the mirror ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T2 fetch update FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc before='$before' after='$after' — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T3: poisoned partial dir is recovered ═══════════════════════════════════
t3() {
  local d="$WORK/t3"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  mkdir -p "$d/mirror.git"          # partial dir left by a killed clone
  echo garbage > "$d/mirror.git/HEAD"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
    ok "T3 poisoned partial dir recovered ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T3 poisoned-dir recovery FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T4: THE INCIDENT — transient fetch failure, clone armed to fail ═════════
# The old logic must NOT pass here: it swallowed the fetch error, recreated
# and died on the failing clone (run 38855793382, exit 128). The fixed
# script must recover via a fetch RETRY with NO recreate at all.
t4() {
  local d="$WORK/t4"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local before
  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
  make_shim "$d/shim" 1 1   # fetch fails once; a clone WOULD fail once
  use_shim "$d/shim"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  use_shim ""
  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
      ok "L1 legacy died on the incident (rc=$rc) — repro confirmed"
    else
      bad "L1 legacy unexpectedly SURVIVED the incident — repro is broken"
    fi

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). - **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

```bash

bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

or pull the script pinned to the run's commit:

```bash
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
```

Either keeps the resilient logic in this single reviewed script while removing the first-run failure mode.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: same first-run failure mode at the `build-ios` mirror step**

Identical root cause as the `build-macos.yml` thread on this PR: this is the first step of the `build-ios` job with no checkout before it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` reads from the persisted workspace of the **previous** run — a pre-merge tree on the first run after merge — and the step dies exit 127. The `submit-ios` step at line 1059 has the same shape. Both legs go red once; gh-1644 stays open.

Apply the same bootstrap fix at both call sites (script extracted from the freshly-updated mirror, or fetched pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com) so no workspace content is assumed before checkout.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1644: the old inline single-shot logic died on the first network
      # hiccup — the recreate fell through to a full `git clone --mirror`
      # whose ~1 h transfer ended in "error: 2931 bytes of body are still

      # fetch with VISIBLE stderr, aborts stalled attempts, and recreates
      # BLOBLESS (--filter=blob:none, the gh-1477 precedent) with retries and
      # partial-dir cleanup. Contract: scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
      # gh-1665 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
      # self-hosted runners — the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
      # wiped), so the script is bootstrapped from the commit-pinned raw URL
      # (workflow_dispatch-only workflows ⇒ ${{ github.sha }} is always a
      # pushed commit) with the mirror copy as the no-network fallback.
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"
          MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — falling back to the mirror copy" >&2
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }

          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git \
            "$MIRROR"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors

          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"

          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/"
          fi

    # = 120m. The old 45m killed healthy slow submits mid-wait (the exact
    # failure #351 was filed for); a genuinely wedged job is still bounded
    # server-side at 120m, and the daily testflight watch budget (240m)
    # covers the whole version→build-ios(90)→submit-ios(120) chain.
    timeout-minutes: 120
    if: needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          # gh-1644: shared resilient updater — fetch retries + blobless
          # recreate with partial-dir cleanup (was single-shot; run
          # 38855793382 died exit 128 on a mid-clone network drop).
          # gh-1665 review: first step of the job, before any checkout —
          # the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree, so bootstrap the
          # script from the commit-pinned raw URL (mirror copy as the
          # no-network fallback), never from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — falling back to the mirror copy" >&2
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Download IPA artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: flutter_app/ipa/

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1644 — update_git_mirror.sh self-test                                  ║

# ║  expected"): the old inline workflow logic fetched ONCE (stderr            ║
# ║  swallowed), fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h       ║
# ║  transfer died mid-flight, and had no retry and no partial-dir cleanup.   ║
# ║  Scenarios (local file:// fixture remotes, fault-injected `git` shim):    ║
# ║    T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror                                ║
# ║    T2 fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits                     ║
# ║    T3 a poisoned partial mirror dir is recovered (recreate)               ║
# ║    T4 THE INCIDENT: transient fetch failure + armed clone failure —       ║
# ║        a fetch RETRY must recover with NO recreate (the legacy logic      ║
# ║        recreated, hit the failing clone and died exit 128)                ║
# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║
# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║
# ║    T7 fetch-retry exhaustion falls back to a successful recreate          ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy
#   --legacy runs the incident scenarios against the PRE-FIX inline
#   workflow logic (embedded below, verbatim behavior of the old
#   build-macos.yml step): every scenario PASSES iff the legacy logic
#   FAILS the contract — i.e. the bug is reproduced. Zero legacy failures
#   means the repro is broken.

cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
MODE="${1:-}"
SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  echo "❌ $SCRIPT missing — run this selftest from the repo root" >&2
  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong
# (the wrapper re-resolves `git` via PATH back into the shim) and spin.
# `command -v -p` resolves against the system default PATH.
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi

pass=0
fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"
  if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
    git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
  else
    if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
    fi
  fi
}

update_mirror() {
  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
  else
    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
  fi
}

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {
  local dir="$1" fail_fetch="$2" fail_clone="$3"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  echo "$fail_fetch" > "$dir/fetch_left"
  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"
  cat > "$dir/git" <<SHIM
#!/usr/bin/env bash
REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
sub=""; skip=0
for a in "\$@"; do
  if [ "\$skip" = 1 ]; then skip=0; continue; fi
  case "\$a" in
    -c|-C) skip=1 ;;
    -*) ;;
    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;
  esac
done
case "\$sub" in
  fetch)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/fetch_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
  clone)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/clone_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
esac
exec "\$REAL_GIT" "\$@"

  chmod +x "$dir/git"
}

use_shim() {  # $1 = shim dir ("" = restore real git)
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then PATH="$1:$REAL_PATH"; else PATH="$REAL_PATH"; fi
}

# ── fixture: a local bare "origin" ──────────────────────────────────────────
make_fixture() {
  local d="$1"
  git init -q "$d/work"
  git -C "$d/work" config user.email t@example.com
  git -C "$d/work" config user.name t
  echo one > "$d/work/file.txt"
  git -C "$d/work" add .
  git -C "$d/work" commit -qm one
  git clone -q --bare "$d/work" "$d/remote.git"
}

advance_fixture() {  # $1 = fixture root — one more commit on the remote
  git -C "$1/work" commit -qm "two-$RANDOM" --allow-empty
  git -C "$1/work" push -q "$1/remote.git" HEAD
}

mirror_head() { git -C "$1" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | head -1; }

export REAL_PATH="$PATH"
export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0

# ══ T1: fresh clone creates a working mirror ════════════════════════════════
t1() {
  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
    ok "T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T1 fresh clone FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T2: fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits ═════════════════════
t2() {
  local d="$WORK/t2"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local before after
  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")

  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  after=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$before" != "$after" ]; then
    ok "T2 fetch advances the mirror ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T2 fetch update FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc before='$before' after='$after' — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T3: poisoned partial dir is recovered ═══════════════════════════════════
t3() {
  local d="$WORK/t3"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  mkdir -p "$d/mirror.git"          # partial dir left by a killed clone
  echo garbage > "$d/mirror.git/HEAD"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
    ok "T3 poisoned partial dir recovered ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T3 poisoned-dir recovery FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T4: THE INCIDENT — transient fetch failure, clone armed to fail ═════════
# The old logic must NOT pass here: it swallowed the fetch error, recreated

  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")

    else
      bad "L1 legacy unexpectedly SURVIVED the incident — repro is broken"

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

(If the runner were instead configured to wipe the workspace, the step fails the same way — only a post-merge workspace makes this line work.)

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

```bash
# mirror already ensured + fetched inline above
git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

or pull the script pinned to the run's commit:

```bash
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
```

Either keeps the resilient logic in this single reviewed script while removing the first-run failure mode.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: same first-run failure mode at the `build-ios` mirror step**

Identical root cause as the `build-macos.yml` thread on this PR: this is the first step of the `build-ios` job with no checkout before it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` reads from the persisted workspace of the **previous** run — a pre-merge tree on the first run after merge — and the step dies exit 127. The `submit-ios` step at line 1059 has the same shape. Both legs go red once; gh-1644 stays open.

Apply the same bootstrap fix at both call sites (script extracted from the freshly-updated mirror, or fetched pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com) so no workspace content is assumed before checkout.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then

  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"

rm -rf "$tmp"

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

env:
      # Workaround: force .NET (used by the runner) to use SocketsHttpHandler
      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1644: the old inline single-shot logic died on the first network
      # hiccup — the recreate fell through to a full `git clone --mirror`
      # whose ~1 h transfer ended in "error: 2931 bytes of body are still
      # expected" (run 38855793382, exit 128). The shared script retries the
      # fetch with VISIBLE stderr, aborts stalled attempts, and recreates
      # BLOBLESS (--filter=blob:none, the gh-1477 precedent) with retries and
      # partial-dir cleanup. Contract: scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
      # gh-1665 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
      # self-hosted runners — the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
      # wiped), so the script is bootstrapped from the commit-pinned raw URL
      # (workflow_dispatch-only workflows ⇒ ${{ github.sha }} is always a
      # pushed commit) with the mirror copy as the no-network fallback.
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"
          MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — falling back to the mirror copy" >&2
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git \
            "$MIRROR"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/"
          fi

# ║        recreated, hit the failing clone and died exit 128)                ║
# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║
# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║
# ║    T7 fetch-retry exhaustion falls back to a successful recreate          ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy

cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
MODE="${1:-}"
SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  echo "❌ $SCRIPT missing — run this selftest from the repo root" >&2
  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong
# (the wrapper re-resolves `git` via PATH back into the shim) and spin.
# `command -v -p` resolves against the system default PATH.
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi

pass=0
fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"
  if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
    git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
  else
    if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
    fi
  fi
}

update_mirror() {
  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
  else
    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
  fi
}

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {
  local dir="$1" fail_fetch="$2" fail_clone="$3"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  echo "$fail_fetch" > "$dir/fetch_left"
  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
sub=""; skip=0
for a in "\$@"; do
  if [ "\$skip" = 1 ]; then skip=0; continue; fi
  case "\$a" in
    -c|-C) skip=1 ;;
    -*) ;;
    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;
  esac
done
case "\$sub" in
  fetch)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/fetch_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
  clone)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/clone_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
esac
exec "\$REAL_GIT" "\$@"

  chmod +x "$dir/git"
}

use_shim() {  # $1 = shim dir ("" = restore real git)
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then PATH="$1:$REAL_PATH"; else PATH="$REAL_PATH"; fi
}

# ── fixture: a local bare "origin" ──────────────────────────────────────────
make_fixture() {
  local d="$1"
  git init -q "$d/work"
  git -C "$d/work" config user.email t@example.com
  git -C "$d/work" config user.name t
  echo one > "$d/work/file.txt"
  git -C "$d/work" add .
  git -C "$d/work" commit -qm one
  git clone -q --bare "$d/work" "$d/remote.git"
}

advance_fixture() {  # $1 = fixture root — one more commit on the remote
  git -C "$1/work" commit -qm "two-$RANDOM" --allow-empty
  git -C "$1/work" push -q "$1/remote.git" HEAD
}

mirror_head() { git -C "$1" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | head -1; }

export REAL_PATH="$PATH"
export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0

# ══ T1: fresh clone creates a working mirror ════════════════════════════════
t1() {
  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
    ok "T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T1 fresh clone FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T2: fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits ═════════════════════
t2() {
  local d="$WORK/t2"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1

  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")

    ok "T3 poisoned partial dir recovered ($(label_legacy))"

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

(If the runner were instead configured to wipe the workspace, the step fails the same way — only a post-merge workspace makes this line work.)

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

```bash
# mirror already ensured + fetched inline above
git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

or pull the script pinned to the run's commit:

```bash
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
```

Either keeps the resilient logic in this single reviewed script while removing the first-run failure mode.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: same first-run failure mode at the `build-ios` mirror step**

Identical root cause as the `build-macos.yml` thread on this PR: this is the first step of the `build-ios` job with no checkout before it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` reads from the persisted workspace of the **previous** run — a pre-merge tree on the first run after merge — and the step dies exit 127. The `submit-ios` step at line 1059 has the same shape. Both legs go red once; gh-1644 stays open.

Apply the same bootstrap fix at both call sites (script extracted from the freshly-updated mirror, or fetched pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com) so no workspace content is assumed before checkout.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then

  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"

rm -rf "$tmp"

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

env:
      # Workaround: force .NET (used by the runner) to use SocketsHttpHandler
      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1644: the old inline single-shot logic died on the first network
      # hiccup — the recreate fell through to a full `git clone --mirror`
      # whose ~1 h transfer ended in "error: 2931 bytes of body are still
      # expected" (run 38855793382, exit 128). The shared script retries the
      # fetch with VISIBLE stderr, aborts stalled attempts, and recreates
      # BLOBLESS (--filter=blob:none, the gh-1477 precedent) with retries and
      # partial-dir cleanup. Contract: scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
      # gh-1665 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
      # self-hosted runners — the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
      # wiped), so the script is bootstrapped from the commit-pinned raw URL
      # (workflow_dispatch-only workflows ⇒ ${{ github.sha }} is always a
      # pushed commit) with the mirror copy as the no-network fallback.
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"
          MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — falling back to the mirror copy" >&2
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git \
            "$MIRROR"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/"
          fi

# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║

# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║

cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
MODE="${1:-}"
SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"

  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong

REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi

pass=0
fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"
  if [ ! -d "$mirror" ]; then
    git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
  else
    if ! git -C "$mirror" fetch origin 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "Fetch failed — recreating mirror: $mirror"
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      git clone --mirror "$url" "$mirror"
    fi
  fi
}

update_mirror() {
  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
  else
    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
  fi
}

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {
  local dir="$1" fail_fetch="$2" fail_clone="$3"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  echo "$fail_fetch" > "$dir/fetch_left"
  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
sub=""; skip=0
for a in "\$@"; do
  if [ "\$skip" = 1 ]; then skip=0; continue; fi
  case "\$a" in
    -c|-C) skip=1 ;;
    -*) ;;
    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;
  esac
done
case "\$sub" in

    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/fetch_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/fetch_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;
  clone)
    if [ "\$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left")" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo \$(( \$(cat "\$LEFT/clone_left") - 1 )) > "\$LEFT/clone_left"
      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2
      exit 128
    fi ;;

use_shim() {  # $1 = shim dir ("" = restore real git)

}

# ── fixture: a local bare "origin" ──────────────────────────────────────────
make_fixture() {
  local d="$1"
  git init -q "$d/work"
  git -C "$d/work" config user.email t@example.com
  git -C "$d/work" config user.name t
  echo one > "$d/work/file.txt"
  git -C "$d/work" add .
  git -C "$d/work" commit -qm one
  git clone -q --bare "$d/work" "$d/remote.git"
}

advance_fixture() {  # $1 = fixture root — one more commit on the remote
  git -C "$1/work" commit -qm "two-$RANDOM" --allow-empty
  git -C "$1/work" push -q "$1/remote.git" HEAD
}

mirror_head() { git -C "$1" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | head -1; }

export REAL_PATH="$PATH"
export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0

# ══ T1: fresh clone creates a working mirror ════════════════════════════════
t1() {
  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"
  local out rc
  out=$(update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")" ]; then
    ok "T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror ($(label_legacy))"
  else
    bad "T1 fresh clone FAILED ($(label_legacy)): rc=$rc — $out"
  fi
}

# ══ T2: fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits ═════════════════════
t2() {
  local d="$WORK/t2"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"

    ok "T3 poisoned partial dir recovered ($(label_legacy))"

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

(If the runner were instead configured to wipe the workspace, the step fails the same way — only a post-merge workspace makes this line work.)

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

```bash
# mirror already ensured + fetched inline above
git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

or pull the script pinned to the run's commit:

```bash
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
```

Either keeps the resilient logic in this single reviewed script while removing the first-run failure mode.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: same first-run failure mode at the `build-ios` mirror step**

Identical root cause as the `build-macos.yml` thread on this PR: this is the first step of the `build-ios` job with no checkout before it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` reads from the persisted workspace of the **previous** run — a pre-merge tree on the first run after merge — and the step dies exit 127. The `submit-ios` step at line 1059 has the same shape. Both legs go red once; gh-1644 stays open.

Apply the same bootstrap fix at both call sites (script extracted from the freshly-updated mirror, or fetched pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com) so no workspace content is assumed before checkout.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then

  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
  echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"

rm -rf "$tmp"

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror
